title: Transform Point/Segment
content: **List of Contents** Transform Point/Segment Rotating Segment Scaling Segment Scaling Segment with Pivot Point Activated Moving Point/Segment **Transform Point/Segment** \- Move, rotate and scale point and segment. \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and hold down the **Edit Pattern** tool as the**Transform Point/Segment** tool will appear below. **Rotating Segment** * **Rotating Segment** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be rotated. \- The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. \- Hover the mouse over the scale point on top of the marquee box. The mouse cursor will appear as a rotating wheel. \- Click and drag the scale point towards the desired direction. \- The segment will rotate around its center. * **Rotating Segment with Pivot Point Activated** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be rotated. \- The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. \- Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. \- The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. \- Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where the selected segment’s rotation should be centered on. \- Hover over the scale point on top of the marquee box. The mouse cursor will appear as a rotating wheel. \- Click and drag the scale point towards the desired direction. \- The selected segment will rotate accordingly centering on the Pivot Point. **Scaling Segment** * **Scaling Segment Manually ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be scaled. \- The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. \- Click one of the scale points and drag towards the selected segment to be scaled. * **Scaling Segment with specific value ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be scaled. \- The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. \- Click one of the scale points and drag towards the selected segment to be scaled. \- As holding down the scale point, right click on the mouse. The Transform pop-up window will appear. \- Type in desired PERCENTAGE and DIMENSION, and then hit OK. \- The selected segment will be scaled accordingly. **Scaling Segment with Pivot Point Activated** * **Scaling Segment Manually ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be scaled. \- The selected segment will be highlighted as a marquee box appears. \- Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. \- The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. \- Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where it will be the center of the transformation. \- Click one of the scale points and drag towards the segment to be scaled. \- The selected segment will be lengthened or shortened centering on the Pivot Point. * **Scaling Segment with specific value ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click on the segment to be scaled. \- The selected segment will be highlighted as a marquee box appears. \- Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. \- The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. \- Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where it will be the center of the transformation. \- Click one of the scale points and drag towards the segment to be scaled. \- As holding down the scale point, right click on the mouse. The Transformation pop-up window will appear. \- Type in desired PERCENTAGE and DIMENSION, then hit OK. \- The selected segment will be lengthened or shortened centering on the Pivot Point. **Moving Point/Segment** * **Moving Point/Segment Manually ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click and drag the point/segment to be moved. \- Move the point/segment to desired place in the 2D Window and release the mouse to complete the movement. * **Moving Point/Segment with specific value ** \- Select the **Transform Point/Segment** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click and drag the point/segment to be moved. \- As holding down the point/segment, right click on the mouse. The Moving Distance pop-up window will appear. \- Type in desired value and hit OK. \- The point/segment will be moved accordingly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to effectively transform, rotate, scale, and move points and segments using the Transform Point/Segment tool in a 2D design environment.

title: How can I delete my account?

title: Failures Caused by Faulty GPU Drivers
content: _Last updated in May 2025 and will be continued until the faulty GPU driver issue is fully resolved._ This article explains how to workaround malfunctions in the CLO software caused by Nvidia graphics card drivers released between December 2024 and March 2025. This issue only occurs on Windows PCs with Nvidia graphics cards and the latest drivers, Macs are not affected. Since 2019, the CLO team has been testing compatibility with Nvidia drivers which released monthly before and after the official release of CLO software on Windows computers equipped with various types of Nvidia graphics cards, and among the recently released drivers, CLO team have determined that the drivers released between September and October 2024 are relatively stable. **Starting with CLO 2025.0.148, released on April 30th, 2025, improvements have been made to mitigate crashes caused by this driver issue**. The latest CLO software will continue to operate stably even under the latest Nvidia driver, but if the issue persists, [**please let the CLO team know**](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus/technical). ## **Problem Situations** * Unable to run CLO software * Crash while launching CLO software * CLO function icon not displayed normally * 2D/3D visual glitches that have never occurred before * Crash or hangups while opening certain project files * Crash or hangups while running 3D simulation * Crash or hangups while vray-rendering ## **How to Workaround** Go to **[Nvidia website (link)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/)** , then download and install drivers released between September and October 2024. In simple terms, it is a rollback to the older driver that was released a few months ago. The CLO team's testing results show that the driver released at that time is stable. ### Detailed Procedures (Recommended) **1** Completely close any applications you use, including CLO software. **2** Check the model name and driver version of your Nvidia graphics card. * You can find your graphics card name in the **Performance** section of **Windows Task Manager**. * You can also check the installed Nvidia graphics driver version in **Programs and Features** in the **Windows Control Panel**. **3** If you have driver installed that was released after December 2024, before uninstalling it, download the drivers released between September and October 2024 from the **[Nvidia website](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/)**. * Make sure to check whether your computer is a desktop or laptop, and whether it is a Geforce or an RTX (Quadro) series before searching. * Do not install the downloaded driver right away, but go to the next step. **4** Uninstall the currently installed Nvidia graphics driver from **Programs and Features** in the **Windows Control Panel**. Depending on the state of Windows and your PC system, a reboot may be required. **5** Install the downloaded driver with **administrator rights**. Right-click on the driver file, select **Run as Administrator** from the context menu that appears, and follow the on-screen instructions. ## **Further Reading** * <https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/forums/game-ready-drivers/13/556258/geforce-grd-57216-feedback-thread-released-13025/> * <https://www.reddit.com/r/pcmasterrace/comments/1iigzpy/is_nvidias_57216_driver_incredibly_unstable_and/?rdt=34874> * <https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102219> ## **Related Troubleshooting Articles** * [CLO System Requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2025) * [Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting) * [Troubleshooting: problems upon vray-rendering](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44373505604889-Troubleshooting-problems-upon-vray-rendering)
content_description: This webpage provides essential workarounds and guidance for resolving CLO software malfunctions on Windows PCs caused by specific Nvidia graphics card drivers released between December 2024 and March 2025.

title: Set Default Files
content: Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. #### 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶**Default Files** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Project** | Define the file path for the default file that is loaded when starting the program. **Save with Thumbnail (PNG)** | ## ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44192924896153) By default, only the project(ZPRJ)/garment(ZPAC) file is saved without a separate thumbnail image (PNG), and it is immediately previewed as a file thumbnail. ![File Explorer.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44195781411097) **📝 ****Note:** The thumbnail image can be saved alogn with the project file if needed. **Current Viewpoint** | Save thumbnail images based on the current 3D viewpoint. **4 Viewpoints** | Save thumbnails as multi-view images from 4 viewpoints (front, right, back, left). The 3D viewpoint is automatically adjusted to fit the garment, not all objects. **Custom Viewpoints** | Open a multi-view snapshot file (MVS) and save it according to the set options. **Avatar ** | **Permission File** | Define Avatar Permission(AVTP) or Alvanon Permission (APF) File's file path. **Material** | **Fabric** | Define the file path for the default fabric physical properties file (PSP). **Texture Images** | ** Open from ** | Assign the default path to load texture images. ** Refresh from Custom Folder Path ** | Define the file path to be used when refreshing textures. **Simulation Property** | Define the file path for the default simulation property (MSTP) file. **Auto Save** | **Time Interval (min)** | Adjust the time interval for auto-saving. **File ****Type/Path** | Define the file type and the saving path for auto-saved files. **Custom Color Palette** | Define the file path for the default color palette (ACO) file. **Garment Information** | Define the file path for the default garment information file.
content_description: Customize your software experience by adjusting default settings in User Settings, ensuring that your preferences are applied every time you restart the application.

title: Washing File (JEAN) of Jeanologia Import/ Export
content: **List of Contents** **Import JEAN File** **Export JEAN File** **Objective** Import a washing file(JEAN) of eDesigner, which is an application of [Jeanologia](https://www.jeanologia.com/) offering laser washing solution, and apply it on a garment as a graphic. When exporting a tech pack(JSON), the applied and edited washing can be exported as JEAN file again. **📝Note:** To import or export JEAN file, eDesigner Plugin must be installed on PC. **Location ** **Import JEAN File** 3D/2D Toolbar ▶ [Graphic (3D/2D Pattern) tool](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000483967-%EA%B7%B8%EB%9E%98%ED%94%BD-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) **Export JEAN File** File ▶ Export ▶ **Jean (JEAN)** **Operation ** **Import JEAN File** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated in Location. → **Open File** window appears. ** ** 2. Click JEAN file. → **eDesigner Login** window appears. 3. Enter the ID and PW of eDesigner then click **Login** button. → The washing image is previewed in the**Import JEAN File** window. 4. Refer to the table below and import JEAN file by clicking the desired option. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Apply All** | Automatically identifies the face of the pattern and all washing images of JEAN file are applied. This functions normally by the type of pants, edit the JEAN file exported from CLO in eDesigner, then import it back to apply to the same garment. When a garment and JEAN file are not corresponding, you can miss the washing file or position and scale may not be matching. Import the missing image individually. **OK (Apply a single image)** | Adds a single washing image that appeared in the **Import JEAN file** window. To apply a washing to the double layers like a back pocket of pants, refer to the contents below. 1) Copy the back pattern piece that applied a washing image. 2) Cut the Internal Shape/ Baseline of the pocket in the back pattern piece. 3) Sew the cut pocket pattern piece onto the back pattern again. 4) Delete the original pocket and the remaining pattern pieces. **※Note:** Drag and drop a JEAN file from Library or OS Dialogue to 3D/2D window. ** Export JEAN File** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. → Export File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and name the file, then click **OK**. **※Note:** * Due to eDesigner supports only PNG format, you must export a graphic in PNG. * You can only export a graphic by following the steps: [Graphic Properties ▶ Classification ▶ Wash (Jeanologia)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360049969394-%EA%B7%B8%EB%9E%98%ED%94%BD-%EC%86%8D%EC%84%B1) * Ensure that you do not classify the file as Wash (Jeanologia) to prevent exporting the duplicated file when the same washing is applied to the double layer like the back pocket sewn into the back pattern. * You can set the washing file(JEAN) type to Wash or Breakage. (ver 6.1) [Go back to the List of Contents](-#Click)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on importing and exporting JEAN files for the eDesigner application, enabling users to apply laser washing solutions to garments and manage tech packs efficiently.

title: Omniverse Connector
content: **New in 2025.0** Add Server Create/Join Session Session in Progress Leave Session Easily exchange USD data via Omniverse Connect to enhance collaborative productivity. For more information on NVIDIA and Omniverse, please check out the links below. * [Create NVIDIA account](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) * [Download and install the Omniverse Launcher](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/download/) * [Set the Omniverse server](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/prod_nucleus/prod_nucleus/overview.html) #### **Add Server** You can add Omniverse Nucleus server in CLO. 1. Click Settings » Display » Window » Omniverse Connect in the top menu. 2. Click Omniverse icon » Add Sever, and enter the sever address. #### **Create/Join Session** 1. [ Import a USD file](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29738864727449-USD-File-Import-Export-ver-2024-0#Click1) which from both Omniverse USD Composer and CLO to connect to the session. 2. Open the same file opend in CLO in Omniverse USD Composer » Content Tab. 3. Create a sesstion in Omniverse USD Composer » LIVE Icon → A session is succesfully created, and you are automatically joined that session with the LIVE icon is activated in Omniverse USD Composer. The Live Session Layer is displayed once you are joined the session. 4. Join the session in CLO » Omniverse Connector Window » Omniverse Icon » Join Session. → The layer from the session is added as a Live type in the USD Layer window. The layer will have the same name as the Live Session Layer in Omniverse USD Composer, and be set to the Authoring Layer. #### **Session in Progress** Export files from CLO to Omniverse USD Composer. When a session in Omniverse USD Composer is connected in CLO, you can export your work in CLO to Omniverse USD Composer through the Export to USD Layer feature. The way Omniverse USD Composer updates the work depends on the type of USD layer (USD, LIVE) that the Authoring Layer is set to. 1. Where the Live Session Layer is set as the Authoring Layer, select desired clothing or trims and click on Export to USD Layer from the right mouse button pop-up menu. → The changes of the session layer is directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer. _* Where a USD Layer is set as the Authoring Layer, the selected are exported to the USD file, but not directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer._ 2. To see these changes in the Omniverse USD Composer, click **FETCH** button when the 'Base USD files have been changed' pop-up appears. ![usd_fetch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45594882482841) **📝****Note:** ▪️ If there is no Prim with the same name on the same Prim Path in Omniverse USD Composer, add a new Prim (Append). ▪️ If there is a Prim with the same name in the Prim Path you set for export in Omniverse USD Composer, the changes will be overwritten on that Prim. #### **Leave Session ** You can leave the session that you are in both CLO and Omniverse USD Composer. 1. Click the Omniverse Icon in Omniverse Connector » Leave Session. → The current session ends and the Live mark disappears from the Omniverse icon. The list of session participants disappears. 2. Click the Live Icon in Omniverse USD Composer in CLO » Leave Session. → The current session ends and the Live status is changed to deactivated. The list of session participants disappears. _**✨Tip:** _ Please try out this [USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) we created with CLO and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow.
content_description: Discover how to enhance collaborative productivity by easily creating, joining, and managing sessions in NVIDIA Omniverse with the latest features in version 2025.0.

title: USD Layer Window
content: ## **New in 2025.0** Create/Open Set Options Export #### With USD, a graphics standard file format, you can increase collaboration productivity with a variety of 3D software. You can export clothing, avatars, and accessories with meshes and materials as USD files. You can also import USD files created in other 3D software packages into CLO. A list of layers for the imported file can be found in the USD Layer window. #### #### **Create/Open** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Display ▶ Windows ▶ USD Layer. Or, right-click on the top of the side window, such as Object Browser or Property Editor. Create | Create an USD file \- An USD file is created with the specified path and name, appearing in the USD Layer window. This file will be set as the Authoring Layer. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. ---|--- Open | Import an USD file Clear | Delete all the layers listed in the USD Layer. 2. The list of created or opend USD layers is structured as follows. Authoring Layer | The default layer which is being used at the moment. \- When running Export to USD Layer for clothing, trims, scenes and props, they will be exported to the Authoring Layer. ---|--- Material | The default path where the Materials appear. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. Mesh | The default path where the Mesh appears. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. #### #### **Set Options** 1. Right-click on the layer list to set options if needed. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44171634932377) Set Authoring Layer | Set the selected layer as active. \- The same can be done by double clicking the left mouse button** **This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is already set as the Authoring Layer. \- Where the selected layer is an USDZ (read only) \- Where the selected layer is missing. ---|--- Delete | Deleted the selected layer. This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is the Authoring Layer. Export USDZ from Layer | Export the selected layer as USDZ (read only) Once an USDZ is imported, it cannot be exported again. #### #### **Export** To export your cloth and/or trim assets from CLO as a USD file; select the assets from either 3D or 2D window, and click "Export to USD Layer" of the object context menu to export them to the Authoring Layer. This will update the USD file corresponding to the Authoring Layer. 1. Set export options if needed. Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Single Object | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Include Fur Strand Data | Include the Fur Strand information. Option | Cache Animation | Saves pattern cache animation. **📝****Note:** Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache | Saves avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. **📝****Note:** In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. **📝****Note:** When exporting garment using Export to USD Layer, the exported output will differ depending on the 3D Garment Rendering Style state. If the 3D garment appears in Thick Textured Surface, it will be exported with thickness.

title: Set Graphic Options
content: Set CLO's Graphic Options.![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45588842971289)[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/laMem5VP5ro) 1. Click Setting ▶ User Settings ▶ **Graphic Options** in the top menu. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Antialiasing** | Set how smooth the outlines of objects appear. As the number increases, the outlines become smoother and the rendering speed becomes slower **Use VBOs** | Set the VBOs usage in order to improve the rendering speed. **** **Normal Blending ** | Choose how to blend the normal map. The normal map blending result is reflected in the 3D window and [UV Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053418574-UV-Editor-Mode-ver-6-0-). **Alpha Blending** A method that simulates the normal blending effect using the alpha value. **Partial Derivative** A method of blending the height map using partial derivatives of the normal map. **Whiteout** A technique optimized to reduce the amount of computation and it is a way to preserve detail while maintaining the tendency of a relatively flat normal. **UDN** Compared to Whiteout and Reoriented, the detail of the normal map is slightly reduced but the optimized calculation method is useful for low-end platforms. **Reoriented** A method that preserves the intensity of all mixed normal maps while maintaining the trend of the flat normal map and the details of the complex normal map well. This is the most accurate and slow method by rotating the normal of the detail to match the normal of the base. **Unity** It is the same method as reoriented but the error in certain situations (when two mixed normals are orthogonal) is abandoned and the performance is improved. **Image Resolution Setting** | ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45588844260889) Set the maximum image resolution for the rendering. The Image that exceed the set resolution is downscaled only while rendering to optimize performance. The higher the image resolution, the more memory CLO requires to render and process.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on configuring CLO's graphic options to optimize rendering quality and performance.

title: Avatar IK Joint Mapping
content: ## **New in 2025.0** IK Joint Mapping Set T-Pose Open/Save #### Streamline IK joint mapping for various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. #### #### **IK Joint Mapping** **ℹ️** The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. 1\. Click Main Menu » Avatar » Avatar Editor » **IK Joint** tab. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ![IK.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695503254809) For optional joints, we recommend mapping those indicated in the image if they are present in the avatar to achieve more accurate results. ![IK_Optional.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44698897617177) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** **Auto** If the avatar meets the following conditions, click **![Auto Mapping.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163400089)**at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the CLO avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: **Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman.** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163389593)** **Manual** 1. Click the desired item from the image or list in the IK Mapping tab, then click the joint to be mapped on the avatar. _* Alternatively, you can first click the joint on the avatar and then click an item from the tab._ 2. When ![IK Symmetric.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147316505)**S****ymmetry Mapping** option at the top right is turned on, the corresponding joint on the opposite side is automatically mapped. Note that both sides must be named as follows: **Left_** / **Right_, L_ / R_** , **Left / Right** , **_L / _R** , **_Left / _Right. ** 3. Once all mapping is set up, adjust the [IK pose.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115009052548-Adjust-Avatar-Joints#h_01J90BEJ6RBW7SQZXTSHZZSA80) **✨Tip:** Use the following tips to enhance the motion quality on the target avatar after IK mapping. • Offset Joint: If a specific joint does not align properly, adjust the avatar joints by using [Offset Joint](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/39336772755737-Offset-Avatar-Joint). • Move to Ground: If the avatar is floating above the ground after applying a motion file, right-click on the avatar and click 'Move to Ground'. #### #### **Set T-Pose** Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with CLO avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. 1. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. _If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped._ 2. Click **![Set T-Pose.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147319449)** at the top right. **📝****Note:** • If set correctly, the ![Reset Pose.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44698897618329) button activates, allowing you to check the set T-pose when cilcked. • After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click the Reset Pose button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. #### #### **Open/Save** You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. 1. Click ![Button-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695147320473) **Save** / ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44695163440025)**Open** at the top right to open or save IK data as a _.iks_ file. * IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped.
content_description: Discover the new IK Joint Mapping capabilities in version 2025.0, designed to enhance natural movement for avatars by ensuring seamless compatibility across diverse poses and motions.

title: AI Pose Generator (Beta)
content: **New in 2025.0** **** Effortlessly create avatar poses using keywords or an image. _ ***** AI Pose Generator is being piloted as a Beta service, and may be suspended to provide better service. _ **** 1. Click Avatar ▶ **AI Pose Generator** in the top menu. 2. Generate a pose image by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select the gender, and enter your prompt. **✨ Writing Tips: **Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. ![Comment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587833642521)**Keyword Suggestions** | Suggested keywords will appear as you type to help you complete your prompt. ![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587817802265)**Maintain Prompt** | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI pose image is created anew each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while preserving the existing results as much as possible. The results may differ from the existing ones depending on the addition or change of the prompts. ![icon_random_dice.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587833646873) **Random** | Sample prompts are provided randomly **Image** | Click the **Upload** button to load a pose image that fits the following guidelines: A full-body image from head to toe is highly recommended to ensure the highest quality of the AI Pose. 3. Click **![Generate.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45588063371673)** Button to generate the pose based on your image. It may take a while to create when there are many users at the same time. 4. Click ![Save.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45588079659033) Button to save the generated pose as the *.pos file.

title: Stress Map
content: \- The **Stress Map** shows any stress applied onto garments; check the force along the fabric grain per unit area on garments. \- Hover over the third icon in the Vertical Toggle Menu in the 3D window. Then, Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001846908/CLT_Group_06Strain_Normal.png)**Stress Map** icon. \- Any part not under stress will appear in blue, but under stress, that part of the garment will turn closer to red. \- There is a common misconception that Stress is Pressure. For evaluating external pressure being applied to the avatar, please use the [Pressure Map](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000436368-Garment-Fit-Maps) instead.
content_description: Explore the **Stress Map** to visualize stress distribution on garments, identifying areas under tension and clarifying the difference between stress and pressure in fabric evaluation.

title: Topstitch Item/Property
content: **List of Contents** Topstitch Item Topstitch Item List Editing Topstitch Item Utilizing Topstitch Item **Topstitch Item ** \- Create and edit Topstitch items. \- Navigate to Object Browser – **Topstitch** Tab ******Topstitch Item List** \- Default_Topstitch is part of the program asset which is created upon download. It is fixed in the list and cannot be deleted. * **Adding Topstitch Item ** \- Navigate to Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **Add** Button \- A new Topstitch item is created. * **Duplicating Topstitch Item **\- Click on the Topstitch item to be duplicated. \- The **Copy** button above the Topstitch List is activated. \- Click the Copy button as a duplicated Topstitch will be created at the bottom of the list. * **Deleting Topstitch Item ** \- Only unused Topstitch item can be deleted. \- Click on the **Delete** icon located at the right side of the Topstitch item. \- Or right-click on the Topstitch item to access the pop-up menu. Select **Delete.** **Editing Topstitch Item** \- Select the Topstitch item to be edited and navigate to Object Browser. * **Name ** \- Change name for the selected Topstitch item. * **Type ** \- There are two types of Topstitches: **OBJ** and **Texture**. ** -** Select desired option. * **Material ** * **Preset** \- Select shapes of Topstitches among provided options: **Custom** , **Bartack** , **Buttonhole** , **Overlock** ,**Pickstitch** , **Single** , **Single_Offset_0** , **Zigzag**. \- When either Buttonhole or Overlock is selected, an additional option **Stitch Width** will appear. * **Color** \- Click on the color chip to change Topstitch color. \- Click on the drop-down arrow next to **Color** to access child options: **Ambient Intensity** and **Diffuse Intensity.** \- Adjust each option as needed. * **Offset** \- Commonly used offset values are provided as preset. \- Input specified value as needed. \- The unit corresponds to the unit that is currently used in CLO. * **Length(SPI)** \- Adjust the length of each Stitch. \- **SPI** is the abbreviation for Stitch per Inch. As SPI increases, each Stitch length shortens. \- Input specified stitch length as needed. * **Thread Thickness** \- Adjust the Thickness of the Thread manually. \- Expand the drop down menus by clicking the Arrow button. \- Choose the desired unit used for Thread Thickness among Tex, Ticket (Tkt,) Metric (Nm,) Denier (Den,) and Millimeter. \- When Preset is set as **Pickstitch** , a child option is added to adjust distance in between each Stitch. * **Face** \- Choose the Topstitch’s placement on the fabric: **Front** , **Back** , **Both** * **Number of Line** \- Assign number of lines for a Topstitch item. \- When more than two lines are created, a child option **Distance** will appear. Use this option to adjust the apart distance of lines. \- Select among provided values or input custom values as needed. * **Multilayered Topstitch ** \- When a Topstitch item is created, only one layer is created by default. \- To create multilayered Topstitch, click the + tab next to 1 tab. \- Toggle On **Use This Stitch** option. The options will be activated. \- Adjust options as needed. \- As many as five layers of Stitches can be created to express complicated Stitch styles such as Color Overlock. * **Multilayered Topstitch_ver.4.1.0 and Above ** \- Create various different types of Topstitches up to five at a time. \- Choose the desired number of Topstitch lines using the drop down menu next to Stitch Count. \- To configure multiple lines of a single Topstitch style at the same time, toggle on below options as needed. \- **Use Same Specification** : Toggle on this option to configure multiple topstitches' Specification related options such as Shape, Length, Space and more at the same time. \- **Use Material** : Toggle on this option to configure multiple topstitches' Material related options such as Texture, Color, Type and more at the same time. * **Default Topstitch Tread Thickness Unit_ver.4.2.0 and avobe ** \- Change the default unit for Topstitch thickness. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ User Interface ▶ Default Topstitch Thread Thickness Unit \- Select the desired unit among five options. * **Space_ver.4.2.0 and avobe ** \- Set the distance between each stitch of Topstitch style. \- The Space value can be both negative and positive values. **Utilizing Topstitch Item ** * **Saving/Opening Topstitch Item ** \- Select the Topstitch item to be saved. \- Click on the **Save** button at the top of the properties. \- A file browser will appear. Designate file name and path, and then click on the **Save** button. \- The Topstitch item will be saved as .sst format. \- To open a Topstitch item, select the **Open** button at the top of the properties. \- When a file browser appears, located and open the Topstitch item to be opened. * **Applying Topstitch Item ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024511568/mceclip0.png) **Edit Topstitch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Then, navigate to 2D window and select on the Topstitch line created on 2D Pattern. The selected Topstitch line will be highlighted in pink. \- Click **Assign** button. \- The selected Topstitch item will be applied to the Topstitch line created on 2D Pattern. \- Or right-click on the Topstitch line on 2D Pattern to access a pop-up menu. \- Select **Assign** to New Topstitch. \- A new Topstitch item is created as it is automatically assigned to the selected Topstitch line on 2D Pattern. ([Reference Editing Topstitch](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013749468)) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, editing, duplicating, and managing Topstitch items within the software, providing users with step-by-step instructions and options for customization.

title: Compatible File Format
content: **Compatible File Format **** ** **File** | **Format** | **Import** | **Export** | **Detail** ---|---|---|---|--- **3D** | **FBX** | *.fbx | O | O | File contains Mesh, Material, Joint, Animation, and Camera information. **COLLADA** | *.dae | O | X | This file can be exported from other 3D softwares such as 3ds Max, Maya, Pose, and DAZ Studio and used. These files contain geometry and material, also in a addition to rigging, skinning, and animation data When exporting COLLADA files from 3DS Max or Maya, install the “OpenCOLLADA plugin ([http://www.opencollada.org/download.html](http://www.opencollada.org/download.html)) and export to use the avatar **OBJ** | *.obj | O | O | File contains Geometry and Material Information. Primarily used for importing Avatar and related sources into the program. **LXO** | *.lxo | X | O | File contains Geometry and Material Information. Used to export Apparel/Avatar information to Modo in the LXO file format. **Animation Cache** | *.mc *.pc2 *.mdd | O | O | Is the vertex animation data. It is possible to take animations made in CLO 3D to 3DSMax or Maya in point cache format. **Alembic** | *.abc | O | O | Is an interchange file format for computer graphics that saves both vertex and animation information. **2D** | **DXF-AAMA** | *.dxf *.aam | O | O | Is the standard format of industry CAD patterns and contains 2D Pattern information. CLO 3D is currently compatible with DXF files such as YUKA, Gerber, Lextra, StyleCAD, Optitex, and Pad System **DXF-ASTM** | *.dxf | O | O **Texture** | *.jpg, *.png, etc. | O | O | Textures inserted into garments, use image textures in formats such as JPG, PNG, TIF, and PSD. Supported file types: jpg, jpeg, png, bmp, wbmp, psd, ico, tga, tif, tiff, gif, mng, jng, dds, hdr, koa, lbm, iff, pbm, pcd, pcx, pgm, ppm, ras, cut, xmb, xpm, sgi, g3, exr, j2k, jp2, pfm, pict, pct) ※Note: Texture files compatible with V-ray Render are: hdr, exr, png, bmp, tga, sgi, jpg, pic, and psd. (V-ray does not support 32bit format of jpeg.) **2D Snapshot** | *.png | - | O | Ability to export patterns (of the 2D window) in a 1:1 scale PNG file. **3D Snapshot** **3D Multiview** | *.png | - | O | Ability to save single and/or multiple views of the 3D window in the PNG file format. **Video** | *.avi | - | O | Ability to capture and export videos of the 3D window in the AVI file format. ****
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive overview of compatible file formats for importing and exporting various 2D and 3D assets, along with detailed descriptions of each format's capabilities.

title: Fabric
content: **List of Contents** Fabric Add Fabric Item Copy Fabric Item Assign Fabric Item Reset Fabric Item Delete Fabric Item **Fabric ** \- In CLO, Fabric can be created just like how it is created in real life, applying texture to material properties. ** Add Fabric Item** ** ** * **The Add Button** \- Click the Add button on the Object Browser’s Fabric Tab. \- A new Fabric Item will be added to the Object Browser. * **Drag & Drop** \- Drag and Drop the Fabric file from the Desktop to the Object Browser. \- The selected file will be added to the Fabric list as a Fabric Item. * **Add From the Library Window** \- When there is a Fabric file in the Library Window, double-click the Fabric file to open. \- The dialogue will appear to inform the user that the file has been added to the Object Browser. The selected file will be added to the Object Browser as a Fabric Item. **Copy Fabric Item** **** \- Select the Fabric Item to be duplicated from the Object Browser. \- Click the Copy button on the right side of the Fabric Item. \- A new Fabric Item will be added having the same material properties with the selected Fabric Item. **Assign Fabric Item** **** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022307188/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021992087/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and select the Pattern that a new Fabric Item will be applied to. \- Locate and click the Assign button on the right top of the Object Browser. \- A new Fabric Item will be added to the Object Browser and it will be automatically applied to the selected Pattern. **Reset Fabric Item** **** \- Right-click on a Fabric Item which its settings will be reset and select **Reset.** \- All settings such as texture, color, and material properties will be changed to default values. **Delete Fabric Item** **** \- A Fabric Item can be deleted and the Delete icon will appear only when it is not applied to any Pattern. If the fabric Item is applied to any Pattern, it cannot be deleted and the Delete icon will disappear. \- When the Delete icon does not appear next to the Fabric Item to be deleted, resolve the issue by following the steps below: \- Select the Fabric Item to be deleted from the Object Browser. The Patterns applied with the selected Fabric Item will be highlighted in pink. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on any Pattern highlighted in pink. Then, click Select All with Same Property ▶ **Fabric** \- Apply other Fabric Items to the selected Patterns. * **Delete Icon ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022307728/mceclip1.png) **Delete** icon next to the Fabric Item. \- The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser. * **Delete Option from the Right Click Pop-up Menu ** \- Right-click on the Fabric Item to be deleted and select **Delete** from the pop-up window. \- The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser. ** ** * **Delete key on Keyboard ** \- Click the Fabric Item to be deleted and hit the **Delete** key on the keyboard. \- The selected Fabric Item will be deleted from the Object Browser. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for managing fabric items in CLO, including instructions for adding, copying, assigning, resetting, and deleting fabric items in the Object Browser.
